owner.occupation: Insurance broker for outdoor tourism businesses

world.bio: I have placed liability cover for kayak, heli-ski and foraging outfits around British Columbia for about twenty years. I started at a general commercial broker and moved into adventure tourism when a client in Tofino asked whether anyone understood whale-watching exposures. I read every incident report that crosses my desk, which my wife says is a strange hobby.
skills_assets: Access to six specialty liability underwriters for guiding and outfitter businesses
Twenty years of incident-report reading: knows which operators lose cover and why
Can draft risk-management protocols that underwriters will actually read
Network of guides, lodge owners and outfitters across BC and Alberta
Home office in Kitsilano with a very good espresso machine

projects.name: Renewal season for the heli-ski and kayak book
projects.text: Forty-two renewals between October and January. Two underwriters have tightened wording on avalanche-related claims; one has dropped coverage for night paddling. I'm sitting down with each client to walk through what changed.

projects.name: Parents' 50th anniversary
projects.text: Planning dinner for forty at a restaurant in Kelowna on November 8. My sister keeps changing the guest list. I have the slideshow half built from scanned slides my father shot in the seventies.

projects.name: Food bank Saturdays
projects.text: Third year volunteering at the Mount Pleasant food bank. I run the cold-storage shelves.

notes.text: Knee is at week eleven. The physio says I'm ahead of schedule, which is the first time in my life I've been ahead of anything. Walking the seawall for forty minutes now, with the cane tucked under my arm mostly as decoration.

Call with one of the underwriters in Calgary about a client who runs bear-viewing tours. He asked whether anything in the operation involved food handling. I said just lunch. He said the wording is changing so ask better questions.
Sister texted at 6:50 am: Mum wants a string quartet at the anniversary. Dad says a jukebox. I'm going to split the difference and book a pianist.

Got the new underwriting circular. Foraging operators that include tasting now need a mycologist-verified identification protocol on file before we can even quote. I've got two clients in that line, a mushroom walk outfit on the Sunshine Coast and a small wild-edibles business on Vancouver Island. Neither has anything like it. I wrote the note to both and then sat looking at the page for a while.
Food bank day. We got a pallet of apples from an orchard in Cawston and had to repack them by hand. Dave from the church group told the same joke about pears he's told every week since March.
Physio session. She showed me a step-up exercise I'm supposed to do twenty times a day. Did eight, got the dog out of the room because he thought it was a game.
Reading an incident report from a rafting company in Golden. Nobody was hurt but the guide's decision-making at the rapid was the problem. I will be reading that paragraph again tonight.
Booked the pianist. Sister wants to know if there's a plus-one for her new boyfriend. Told her to ask Mum, I'm not touching that.

messages.text:
Jenny: Please can you confirm the guest count by Friday.
Me: I count thirty-eight and one maybe.
Jenny: Who's the maybe?
Me: Your boyfriend. You haven't said whether he's coming.

Client: Mark, got your note about the new tasting rules. What does mycologist-verified actually mean?
Me: Underwriters want someone with formal training to sign off on how you identify species, not just your own experience.
Client: I've been doing this fifteen years.
Me: I know. I believe you. They don't know you.

Physio: Walking without the cane for short distances now?
Me: Around the house, yes.
Physio: Good. Not the stairs yet.

Dad: Your mother says the slideshow better not have the photo of me in the flares.
Me: It's the best photo.
Dad: That's what I'm afraid of.

calendar.event: Renewal call, heli-ski operator in Revelstoke

relations.about: A client with fifteen years of foraging walks and no formal ID protocol; worried about renewing
Retired high-school shop teacher, 79, shot most of the family's early photos
Food bank volunteer, tells the same pear joke every week

constraints: Not travelling far until the knee is fully recovered
Won't write cover for operators who skip documented risk procedures
Saturdays are for the food bank
sensitive: Worried he will not be as mobile as before the surgery
Has been quietly saving for a trip with his wife that the knee put off
